name: Carrie Brown
summary: Carrie Brown, a prostitute known as 'Old Shakespeare,' was found murdered and mutilated in her New York City hotel room. She was initially suspected as a Jack the Ripper copycat victim but the timing didn't align.

name: Andrew & Abby Borden
summary: Andrew Borden and his wife Abby were found hacked to death in their Fall River, Massachusetts home. Their daughter Lizzie was acquitted of the murders.

name: Stanford White
summary: Prominent architect Stanford White was shot in front of hundreds of witnesses at Madison Square Garden's rooftop restaurant by millionaire Harry K. Thaw, who was enraged over White's past relationship with his wife Evelyn Nesbit.

name: Virginia Christian Case
summary: Seventeen-year-old Virginia Christian became the first woman executed in Virginia's electric chair for the murder of her employer. The case raised questions about juvenile justice and racial disparities.

name: New Orleans Axeman Victims
summary: The New Orleans Axeman murdered at least eight people and attacked several others between 1918 and 1919. He sent a letter to newspapers saying he would spare any household playing jazz music on a particular night.

name: Virginia Rappe
summary: Silent film actress Virginia Rappe died following a party at the St. Francis Hotel in San Francisco. Actor Roscoe 'Fatty' Arbuckle was charged with her rape and murder three times; all trials ended in acquittal or hung jury.

name: William Desmond Taylor
summary: Silent film director William Desmond Taylor was found shot in his bungalow in Los Angeles. The murder implicated several silent film actresses, including Mabel Normand and Mary Miles Minter.

name: Bobby Franks
summary: Fourteen-year-old Bobby Franks was murdered by wealthy University of Chicago students Nathan Leopold and Richard Loeb as a thrill kill. Attorney Clarence Darrow's defense saved them from execution; they received life sentences.

name: Judge Joseph Force Crater
summary: New York Supreme Court Justice Joseph Force Crater disappeared in New York City after dining with friends. He hailed a cab and was never seen again. Despite massive investigation, no trace of him was ever found.

name: Starr Faithfull
summary: Starr Faithfull was found drowned on a Long Beach, New York beach. Her diary revealed an ongoing relationship with politician Andrew James Peters who allegedly abused her.

name: Charles Lindbergh Jr.
summary: The infant son of aviator Charles Lindbergh was kidnapped from the family estate in Hopewell, New Jersey. A ransom was paid but the baby's body was found two months later.

name: Paul Bern
summary: MGM film director Paul Bern was found shot at his Beverly Hills home. It was ruled a suicide but a note was found that some interpret as a murder.

name: Cleveland Torso Murders
summary: The Cleveland Torso Murderer killed at least 12 people in the Kingsbury Run neighborhood of Cleveland between 1934 and 1938. Victims were decapitated and dismembered; most were never identified.

name: Thelma Todd
summary: Actress Thelma Todd was found dead in her garage from carbon monoxide. The death was ruled accidental but many believed it was murder. Theories pointed to her business partner Roland West or mob figure Lucky Luciano.

name: Amelia Earhart
summary: Pioneer aviator Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished over the Pacific Ocean during her attempt to circumnavigate the globe. She was declared legally dead in 1939.

name: Betty June Binnicker & Mary Emma Thames
summary: Two young girls were found murdered in Alcolu, South Carolina. George Stinney Jr., a 14-year-old Black boy, was arrested, tried, and executed in 83 days — the youngest person executed in the 20th century US.

name: Recy Taylor
summary: Recy Taylor, a young Black woman, was gang-raped by six white men while walking home from church in Abbeville, Alabama. Two grand juries refused to indict the perpetrators. Rosa Parks investigated the case for the NAACP.

name: Suzanne Degnan
summary: Six-year-old Suzanne Degnan was abducted from her bedroom in Chicago and dismembered. William Heirens, known as the 'Lipstick Killer' for writing on walls with lipstick, was convicted in 1946 and spent 65 years in prison.

name: Texarkana Moonlight Murders
summary: The Phantom Killer committed five known murders and two attacks in the Texarkana area across the Texas-Arkansas border in 1946. The victims were typically couples in cars on lover's lanes.

name: Elizabeth Short (The Black Dahlia)
summary: The mutilated body of 22-year-old Elizabeth Short was found in a vacant lot in Los Angeles. Her body had been severed at the waist, drained of blood, and posed.

name: Beverly Potts
summary: Ten-year-old Beverly Potts disappeared from a Cleveland park while attending a neighborhood show. Despite one of the largest manhunts in Cleveland history, she was never found.

name: Bobby Greenlease
summary: Six-year-old Bobby Greenlease was kidnapped from his school and killed by Carl Austin Hall and Bonnie Brown Heady in Kansas City. A ransom of $600,000 was paid — the largest at that time.

name: Frank Olson
summary: CIA scientist Frank Olson died after falling from a New York hotel window. It was ruled a suicide but his family believed he was killed because he wanted to leave the agency's secret mind control program MKUltra.

name: Janet Christman
summary: Thirteen-year-old Janet Christman was babysitting when she was raped and strangled in Columbia, Missouri. Her body was found by the parents when they returned home.

name: Marilyn Sheppard
summary: Marilyn Sheppard was bludgeoned to death in her Bay Village, Ohio home. Her husband, Dr. Sam Sheppard, was convicted of murder in 1954 but his conviction was overturned. Retried in 1966, he was acquitted.

name: Emmett Till
summary: Fourteen-year-old Emmett Till, a Black teenager from Chicago, was brutally murdered in Money, Mississippi after allegedly whistling at a white woman. His killers Roy Bryant and J.W.

name: Emmett Till Reexamination (2022)
summary: In 2022, the Department of Justice reopened the Emmett Till murder case after a manuscript revealed that Carolyn Bryant Donham had lied during the 1955 trial. She died in 2023 before any charges could be filed.

name: Barbara & Patricia Grimes
summary: Sisters Barbara (15) and Patricia (13) Grimes disappeared after seeing an Elvis Presley movie in Chicago. Their nude bodies were found in a ditch outside the city weeks later.

name: Daniel Barter
summary: Four-year-old Daniel Barter disappeared from his family home near Perdido Bay, Alabama on June 18, 1959. Despite searches, he was never found. The FBI listed his case as one needing fresh leads.

name: Henry Lee Lucas Victims
summary: Henry Lee Lucas confessed to hundreds of murders but most were unverifiable. He was confirmed in several cases including the murder of his mother and with accomplice Ottis Toole.

name: Boston Strangler Victims
summary: Thirteen women were strangled in the Boston area between 1962 and 1964. Albert DeSalvo confessed to all 13 murders but was never tried for them. DNA evidence collected in 2013 linked DeSalvo to the last victim, Mary Sullivan.

name: William 'Billy' Jones Jr.
summary: Three-year-old William 'Billy' Jones Jr. disappeared from Vineland, New Jersey on December 17, 1962. Despite investigation, he was never found. His case is one of the oldest open missing person cases listed by the FBI.

name: 16th Street Baptist Church Bombing Victims
summary: A KKK bomb killed four young Black girls — Addie Mae Collins, Cynthia Wesley, Carole Robertson, and Carol Denise McNair — at the 16th Street Baptist Church in Birmingham, Alabama. Robert Chambliss was convicted in 1977.

name: Frank Sinatra Jr. Kidnapping
summary: Frank Sinatra Jr. was kidnapped from his hotel room at Harrah's Lake Tahoe on December 8, 1963. A ransom of $240,000 was paid. He was released after three days.

name: John F. Kennedy Assassination
summary: President John F. Kennedy was shot and killed while riding in a presidential motorcade through Dealey Plaza in Dallas. Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested as a suspect but was shot and killed by Jack Ruby two days later before trial.

name: Medgar Evers
summary: Civil rights leader Medgar Evers was shot in the driveway of his Jackson, Mississippi home. White supremacist Byron De La Beckwith was tried twice in 1964 but both trials ended in hung juries.

name: James Chaney, Andrew Goodman & Michael Schwerner
summary: Three civil rights workers disappeared in Neshoba County, Mississippi while investigating the burning of a Black church. Their bodies were found 44 days later.

name: Kitty Genovese
summary: Kitty Genovese was stabbed to death outside her apartment in Kew Gardens, Queens. The case became famous for the 'bystander effect' theory after news reports claimed 38 neighbors heard or witnessed the attack without calling…

name: Alice Crimmins
summary: The two young children of Alice Crimmins — Eddie (age 5) and Missy (age 4) — were discovered dead in Queens, New York in July 1965, just days apart.

name: Jimmie Lee Jackson
summary: Jimmie Lee Jackson was a Black civil rights marcher shot by Alabama State Trooper James Bonard Fowler during a night march in Marion. His death inspired the Selma-to-Montgomery marches and the Voting Rights Act.

name: Cheri Jo Bates
summary: Cheri Jo Bates was found stabbed to death near the library of Riverside City College. The Zodiac Killer sent letters claiming responsibility for the murder, though investigators debated whether it was truly his work.

name: Richard Speck Victims
summary: Richard Speck broke into a Chicago townhouse and methodically murdered eight student nurses. Corazon Amurao survived by hiding under a bed and later identified Speck.

name: Valerie Percy
summary: Valerie Percy, daughter of Senate candidate Charles Percy, was stabbed and beaten to death in her family's lakeside mansion in Kenilworth. A mysterious intruder entered through a window.

name: Barbara Jane Mackle
summary: Barbara Jane Mackle, daughter of a wealthy developer, was kidnapped from an Emory University motel room and buried alive in a ventilated box. Her captors Gary Steven Krist and Ruth Eisemann-Schier demanded ransom.

name: David Faraday & Betty Lou Jensen
summary: David Faraday (17) and Betty Lou Jensen (16) were the Zodiac Killer's first confirmed victims, shot on a dark lover's lane in Benicia, California.

name: Jane Durrua
summary: Thirteen-year-old Jane Durrua was abducted and murdered in Rahway, New Jersey. Robert Zarinsky was convicted of her murder in 2001 using genetic evidence, 33 years after the crime. He was also linked to additional murders.

name: Robert F. Kennedy Assassination
summary: Senator Robert F. Kennedy was shot at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles after winning the California presidential primary. Sirhan Sirhan was convicted and imprisoned.

name: Zodiac Killer Victims
summary: At least five confirmed victims were killed by an unidentified serial killer in Northern California between 1968 and 1969. The killer taunted police and newspapers with cryptic letters and ciphers signed with a crosshair symbol.

name: Bryan Hartnell & Cecelia Shepard
summary: Bryan Hartnell and Cecelia Shepard were attacked by the Zodiac Killer at Lake Berryessa, Napa County. Both were stabbed multiple times; Cecelia died two days later.

name: Charles Manson Victims
summary: Charles Manson directed his followers to commit a series of brutal murders in Los Angeles in August 1969, including actress Sharon Tate. Multiple cult members were convicted.

name: Jane Britton
summary: Harvard graduate student Jane Britton was found bludgeoned to death in her Cambridge apartment. Red ochre was sprinkled on her body.

name: Mary Jo Kopechne
summary: Mary Jo Kopechne drowned when a car driven by Senator Ted Kennedy went off a bridge on Chappaquiddick Island. Kennedy survived and waited nine hours before reporting the accident. He pleaded guilty to leaving the scene.

name: Paul Stine
summary: Cab driver Paul Stine was shot in the back of the head by the Zodiac Killer while stopped in the Presidio Heights neighborhood of San Francisco. The Zodiac sent police a piece of Stine's bloodied shirt to prove his guilt.

name: Sharon Tate & LaBianca Murders
summary: Actress Sharon Tate and four others were murdered at the Polanski home in Bel Air. The next night, Leno and Rosemary LaBianca were killed.

name: Dean Corll Victims
summary: Dean Corll, with accomplices David Brooks and Elmer Wayne Henley, tortured and murdered at least 28 young men and boys in Houston. Corll was shot and killed by Henley in 1973, who then led police to multiple burial sites.

name: Christine Marie Eastin
summary: Nineteen-year-old Christine Marie Eastin disappeared from Hayward, California on January 18, 1971. She was last seen near her home. Despite FBI involvement, she was never found.

name: D.B. Cooper
summary: A man calling himself Dan Cooper hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305 in 1971, extorted $200,000 in ransom, and parachuted from the plane somewhere over the Pacific Northwest. He was never identified or found.

name: List Family Murders
summary: John List murdered his wife, three teenage children, and elderly mother in their Westfield, New Jersey mansion, then vanished for 18 years.

name: Robert Hansen Victims
summary: Robert Hansen was an Anchorage baker who abducted women, flew them to remote Alaska wilderness, and hunted them. He confessed to 17 murders and was convicted in 1984. He died in prison in 2014.

name: Texas Killing Fields Victims
summary: At least 11 women and girls were found dead or disappeared in a stretch of wetlands outside League City, Texas known as the Killing Fields. Only some victims have been identified.

name: Dorothy Hunt
summary: Dorothy Hunt, wife of Watergate figure E. Howard Hunt, was killed in a United Airlines plane crash near Chicago. She was allegedly carrying $10,000 in cash.

name: John Wayne Gacy Victims
summary: John Wayne Gacy tortured and murdered 33 young men and boys, burying 26 under his house. He was convicted in 1980 and executed in 1994. After his execution, investigators used DNA to identify unknown victims.

name: Barbara Gibbons
summary: Barbara Gibbons was found murdered in her Canaan, Connecticut home. Her eighteen-year-old son Peter Reilly was initially convicted based on a coerced confession but later exonerated. The actual killer has never been identified.

name: BTK Killer Victims
summary: Dennis Rader, known as BTK (Bind, Torture, Kill), murdered 10 people in and around Wichita, Kansas between 1974 and 1991. He taunted police and media for decades.

name: Coral Eugene Watts Victims
summary: Coral Eugene Watts confessed to 13 murders in Michigan and Texas. He was convicted of burglary with intent to murder in Texas in 1982 and given a 60-year sentence.

name: Golden State Killer Victims
summary: The Golden State Killer committed at least 13 murders, 50 rapes, and 100 burglaries across California. Joseph James DeAngelo, a former police officer, was identified in 2018 through genealogy DNA testing and pleaded guilty in…

name: Margaret Ellen Fox
summary: Fourteen-year-old Margaret Fox disappeared from Burlington, New Jersey in June 1974. She was last seen near her home. Despite investigation spanning decades, she was never found.

name: Otero Family Murders
summary: The Otero family — Joseph, Julie, Joseph Jr., and Josephine — were bound and murdered in their Wichita home by BTK killer Dennis Rader. This was BTK's first confirmed attack. Rader was not identified for 30 years.

name: Patty Hearst Kidnapping
summary: Newspaper heiress Patty Hearst was abducted from her Berkeley apartment by the Symbionese Liberation Army. After months in captivity she participated in a bank robbery.

name: Ted Bundy Victims
summary: Ted Bundy confessed to 30 homicides across seven states, though the actual number is believed higher. He was executed in Florida in 1989.

name: Ted Bundy Washington Victims
summary: Several of Ted Bundy's earliest confirmed victims disappeared from Washington State in 1974, including Lynda Ann Healy. Bundy attended the University of Washington before his killing spree expanded across the country.

name: David Williams & Steven Anderson
summary: Twelve-year-old David Williams and seventeen-year-old Steven Anderson both disappeared from Pemberton Township, New Jersey on April 7, 1975. Neither was ever found.

name: Jimmy Hoffa
summary: Teamsters Union president Jimmy Hoffa was last seen in a restaurant parking lot in Bloomfield Township, Michigan. He was believed to have been murdered by organized crime figures.

name: Myrna Opsahl
summary: Myrna Opsahl was shot and killed during a bank robbery by members of the Symbionese Liberation Army in Carmichael, California. Patricia Hearst and several SLA members were later convicted of the robbery in 2003 for charges…

name: Robert Lee Yates Victims
summary: Robert Lee Yates Jr. was a decorated Army National Guard helicopter pilot who confessed to 13 murders in eastern Washington and convicted of two in Oregon. He targeted mostly sex workers in Spokane.

name: Anna Mae Aquash
summary: Mi'kmaq activist Anna Mae Aquash was found shot dead on the Pine Ridge Reservation. She had been an American Indian Movement leader.

name: Oakland County Child Killer Victims
summary: A serial killer known as the 'Babysitter' abducted and murdered four children in Oakland County, Michigan. The victims ranged in age from 10 to 12 years old.

name: Son of Sam Victims
summary: David Berkowitz, known as 'Son of Sam,' murdered six people and wounded seven others in New York City over 13 months. He terrorized the city with taunting letters to police and media.

name: Bonnie Garland
summary: Twenty-one-year-old Yale student Bonnie Garland was killed with a hammer by her Yale student boyfriend Richard Herrin while she slept at her parents' Scarsdale home. Herrin claimed he was in a dissociative state.

name: Hillside Strangler Victims
summary: Cousins Angelo Buono and Kenneth Bianchi posed as police officers, kidnapped, raped, and murdered 10 women in Los Angeles. Their victims were found on hillsides, giving rise to the 'Hillside Strangler' name.

name: Roger Kibbe Victims
summary: Roger Kibbe was convicted of murdering seven women in California, known as the I-5 Strangler. His victims were found along freeways.

name: Bob Crane
summary: TV actor Bob Crane, star of Hogan's Heroes, was found bludgeoned to death in his Scottsdale apartment. His acquaintance John Carpenter was tried for the murder in 1994 but acquitted.

name: FSU Chi Omega Murders
summary: Ted Bundy broke into the Chi Omega sorority at Florida State University, killing two women and injuring two others. He also attacked a student at another location that night.

name: Jeffrey Dahmer Victims
summary: Jeffrey Dahmer murdered 17 young men and boys in Wisconsin and Ohio, engaging in necrophilia and cannibalism. He was convicted of 15 murders in Wisconsin and sentenced to 15 life terms.

name: Judy Chartier
summary: Seventeen-year-old Judy Chartier disappeared after leaving a party in Chelmsford, Massachusetts in June 1982. Neither she nor the car she was driving has ever been found.

name: Kimberly Leach
summary: Twelve-year-old Kimberly Leach was the last victim of Ted Bundy, abducted from her middle school in Lake City, Florida. Her remains were found in a pig shed.

name: Rep. Leo Ryan & Jonestown Victims
summary: U.S. Congressman Leo Ryan was shot dead at an airstrip in Guyana along with members of his delegation while investigating Jim Jones's Peoples Temple.

name: Frank Hilley
summary: Frank Hilley died in Anniston, Alabama in 1975 of what was initially diagnosed as infectious hepatitis. After his body was exhumed, his death was attributed to arsenic poisoning, and his wife Audrey Marie Hilley was convicted of…

name: Atlanta Child Murders Victims
summary: At least 28 young Black children and adults were murdered in Atlanta between 1979 and 1981, causing citywide panic. Wayne Williams was convicted of two adult murders and sentenced to life.

name: Etan Patz
summary: Six-year-old Etan Patz was one of the first missing children to appear on a milk carton when he disappeared walking to school in SoHo. The case transformed child safety in America.

name: Susan Reinert
summary: English teacher Susan Reinert was found dead in the trunk of her car in Ardmore with her two children missing and never found. Her colleague and former lover William Bradfield was convicted of her murder, and Dr. Jay C.

name: Wayne Williams Conviction Review
summary: Wayne Williams was convicted in 1982 of two adult murders during the Atlanta Child Murders era. Atlanta police attributed most of the child deaths to him despite no direct evidence.

name: Betty Gore
summary: Betty Gore was found brutally axed to death in her home in Wylie, Texas. Her neighbor and friend, Candy Montgomery, was charged with the murder. Montgomery claimed self-defense and was acquitted in a famous trial.

name: Herman Tarnower
summary: Dr. Herman Tarnower, creator of the Scarsdale Diet, was shot at his Purchase, New York home by his longtime companion Jean Harris. Harris claimed she intended to kill herself but shot him accidentally during a struggle.

name: Jeannie Mills Family
summary: Jeannie Mills, one of the early defectors from Jim Jones's Peoples Temple, was murdered along with her husband Al and their daughter Linda in their Berkeley home. She had been a vocal critic of Jones and Jonestown.

name: Tammy Terrell
summary: An unidentified 17-year-old woman was found dead in Henderson, Nevada in May 1980. She may have been a victim of human trafficking. Despite forensic examination, she was never identified.

name: Adam Walsh
summary: Six-year-old Adam Walsh was abducted from a Sears store in Hollywood, Florida. His severed head was found two weeks later. The case transformed his father John Walsh into a victims' rights advocate who created America's Most…

name: Dean and Tina Clouse
summary: The decomposing remains of Dean and Tina Clouse were found in Houston, Texas in 1981. They had reportedly been associated with a 'Jesus freak' cult. Their infant daughter Lisa was found alive having been abandoned.

name: Keddie Cabin Murders
summary: Glenna Sharp and her son Johnny and family friend Dana Wingate were bound, stabbed, and bludgeoned in Cabin 28 at Keddie resort. The other Sharp children survived by hiding in an adjacent cabin.

name: Marcia King (Buckskin Girl)
summary: Known as 'Buckskin Girl' for the fringed jacket she wore, Marcia King was found murdered along US Route 40 near Troy, Ohio in April 1981. She was unidentified for 37 years until DNA genealogy testing identified her in 2018.

name: Philip Testa
summary: Philadelphia mob boss Philip 'Chicken Man' Testa was killed by a nail bomb planted under his front porch. The bombing sparked a Mafia war within the Philadelphia crime family.

name: Sebastian Russo
summary: Physician Sebastian Russo was shot in his Baltimore office, apparently targeted for prescription drugs. Despite investigation, no suspects were identified or charged. The case remains open in Baltimore Police cold case files.

name: Tammy Mahoney
summary: Nineteen-year-old Tammy Mahoney disappeared from Oneida, New York on May 8, 1981. She was last seen leaving her boyfriend's home.

name: Chicago Tylenol Murders Victims
summary: Seven people in Chicago died after taking cyanide-laced Tylenol capsules in 1982. The deaths prompted a nationwide recall and led to tamper-resistant packaging regulations. James W.

name: Diane Suzuki
summary: Twenty-one-year-old Diane Suzuki disappeared after finishing a class at the Aiea, Hawaii dance studio where she assisted in June 1985. She was never found and was later declared legally dead.

name: Dorothea Puente Victims
summary: Dorothea Puente was a Sacramento boardinghouse operator who poisoned elderly tenants and continued cashing their Social Security checks. Seven bodies were found buried in her yard in 1988.

name: Gary Ridgway Unidentified Victims
summary: Beyond his confirmed 49 victims, Gary Ridgway claimed to have killed as many as 90 women. Several of the confirmed victims were not identified for years.

name: Green River Killer Victims
summary: Gary Ridgway, the Green River Killer, murdered at least 49 women in Washington State. He targeted mostly sex workers and runaways. Ridgway was convicted in 2003 after DNA evidence linked him to four victims.

name: Kathleen McCormack Durst
summary: Kathleen McCormack Durst, wife of real estate heir Robert Durst, disappeared from their South Salem home. Robert Durst was investigated but not charged. He later killed a neighbor in Texas and was acquitted of that murder.

name: Kellie Poppleton
summary: Fourteen-year-old Kellie Poppleton disappeared in Fremont, California on December 2, 1983 and was found murdered hours later. Despite an extensive investigation and periodic reexamination of the evidence, her killer has never…

name: Las Vegas Jane Doe (1982)
summary: An unidentified woman's remains were found in the desert outside Las Vegas in August 1982. She has never been identified. The case is entered in NamUs and Clark County investigators continue to seek her identity.

name: Wah Mee Club Massacre
summary: Thirteen people were robbed and murdered at the Wah Mee private gambling club in Seattle's Chinatown. Ng Wai-chiu, Tony Ng, and Willie Mak committed the massacre.

name: Angela Samota
summary: Twenty-year-old Southern Methodist University student Angela Samota was sexually assaulted and murdered in her Dallas apartment.

name: Night Stalker Victims
summary: Richard Ramirez, the Night Stalker, terrorized Southern California committing 14 murders, rapes, and burglaries. He was captured after residents of Mission Viejo recognized him and held him until police arrived.

name: Vicki Lynne Hoskinson
summary: Eight-year-old Vicki Lynne Hoskinson disappeared while mailing a letter near her Tucson home. Her remains were found eight months later.

name: Grim Sleeper Victims
summary: Lonnie Franklin Jr., known as the Grim Sleeper, was convicted of killing 10 women in Los Angeles between 1985 and 2007. He appeared to stop killing for years (hence 'Grim Sleeper') and was identified through familial DNA from…

name: Shari Smith
summary: Seventeen-year-old Shari Smith was abducted and killed in Saluda County, South Carolina. Larry Gene Bell kidnapped and killed Shari and later a nine-year-old girl, Debra May Helmick. Bell was convicted and executed in 1996.

name: Steve Christensen & Kathy Sheets
summary: Two people were killed by mail bombs in Salt Lake City — Steve Christensen at his office and Kathy Sheets at her home. The next day, the bomber Mark Hofmann was seriously injured when one of his own bombs exploded.

name: Anthonette Christine Cayedito
summary: Nine-year-old Anthonette answered a knock at the door of her family home around 3 AM and was abducted. Her younger sister witnessed two men grab Anthonette and carry her away.

name: Colonial Parkway Murders
summary: Three couples and one woman were murdered along the Colonial Parkway in Virginia between 1986 and 1989. Despite being investigated by the FBI and state police, no one was ever charged.

name: Dorothy Miller
summary: Dorothy Miller was one of Dorothy Puente's victims at the Sacramento boarding house. Her death was among those discovered when seven bodies were found buried in Puente's yard in 1988.

name: Gary Heidnik Victims
summary: Gary Heidnik kidnapped, tortured, and killed women in the basement of his Philadelphia home. He was arrested in 1987 when a victim escaped. Two women died. Heidnik was convicted of first-degree murder and executed in 1999.

name: Jennifer Levin
summary: Jennifer Levin was found strangled in Central Park near the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Her date, Robert Chambers, was suspected in what the tabloids called the 'Preppy Murder.' Chambers pleaded guilty to manslaughter in 1988…

name: Lisa Steinberg
summary: Six-year-old Lisa Steinberg was beaten to death by Joel Steinberg, her illegal adoptive father, in their Greenwich Village apartment. Her abuse had been ongoing.

name: Peggy Hettrick
summary: Peggy Hettrick was found mutilated in a field in Fort Collins. Tim Masters was wrongfully convicted in 1999 and served nine years before his conviction was vacated in 2008 using new DNA and forensic evidence.

name: Amber Swartz
summary: Seven-year-old Amber Swartz disappeared from near her Pinole, California home in June 1988. Despite massive searches and investigation, she was never found.

name: Tara Leigh Calico
summary: Nineteen-year-old Tara Calico went for a bike ride along Highway 47 and never returned. Her bicycle was never found. A year later, a polaroid photo of a bound young woman and boy was found at a Florida convenience store…

name: Aileen Wuornos Victims
summary: Aileen Wuornos killed seven men along Florida highways, claiming self-defense. She was convicted of six murders and executed in 2002.

name: Dan Broderick
summary: Betty Broderick shot and killed her ex-husband attorney Dan Broderick and his new wife Linda in La Jolla. The divorce had been bitter and acrimonious. Betty was convicted and sentenced to 32 years to life.

name: Danny Rolling Confession
summary: Before the Gainesville murders, Danny Rolling murdered three members of the Grissom family in Shreveport, Louisiana in 1989. He confessed to these murders as well. He was eventually executed in 2006 for the Florida murders.

name: Ilene Beth Misheloff
summary: Thirteen-year-old Ilene Misheloff disappeared while walking home from school in Dublin, California. She has never been found. A former neighbor was considered a suspect decades later.

name: Jacob Wetterling
summary: Eleven-year-old Jacob Wetterling was abducted at gunpoint near his home in St. Joseph, Minnesota. His disappearance led directly to the Jacob Wetterling Crimes Against Children and Sexually Violent Offender Registration Act.

name: Lisa Bianco
summary: Lisa Bianco was killed by her abusive ex-husband Alan Matheney in Mishawaka, Indiana. Matheney was on a prison work-release program when he killed her.

name: Robert Ben Rhoades Victims
summary: Robert Ben Rhoades was a long-haul trucker convicted of murdering a couple in 1990. He later confessed to 50 murders along US highways over 15 years. He was convicted of two murders and sentenced to life in Illinois.

name: Gainesville Ripper Victims
summary: Danny Rolling murdered five University of Florida students in three days in Gainesville, Florida. He was sentenced to death and executed in 2006. The murders inspired the film Scream.

name: Paige Renkoski
summary: Twenty-one-year-old Paige Renkoski disappeared while driving near Okemos, Michigan. Her car was found running with her purse inside. A witness reported seeing her talking to a man in another car.

name: Charles Albright Victims
summary: Charles Albright was convicted of one murder in Dallas but suspected in two additional cases. His victims' eyes were always removed post-mortem, earning him the nickname 'The Eyeball Killer.' He was sentenced to life imprisonment.

name: Danny Casolaro
summary: Investigative journalist Danny Casolaro was found dead in a Martinsburg, West Virginia hotel bathtub. His death was ruled suicide.

name: Latasha Harlins
summary: Fifteen-year-old Latasha Harlins was shot and killed by Korean-American store owner Soon Ja Du in Los Angeles. Du was convicted of voluntary manslaughter but given probation and no jail time.

name: Mark Himebaugh
summary: Eleven-year-old Mark Himebaugh disappeared from Del Haven, New Jersey on November 25, 1991. He was playing outside when he vanished. Despite extensive searches and FBI involvement, Mark has never been found.

name: I-70 Killer Victims
summary: Six employees of shoe and sporting goods stores were shot in April-May 1992 along Interstate 70 in Kansas, Missouri, and Indiana. All victims were shot from close range in the back of the head.

name: Jeremy Guillory
summary: Six-year-old Jeremy Guillory was lured into the home of convicted sex offender Ricky Langley and strangled in Iowa, Louisiana. Langley confessed but has been tried three times due to procedural issues, receiving varying sentences.

name: Phoenix Jane Doe (1992)
summary: An unidentified woman's remains were found in the desert east of Phoenix, Arizona in October 1992. She has never been identified despite forensic examination.

name: Springfield Three
summary: Sherrill Levitt, her daughter Suzanne Streeter, and Suzanne's friend Stacy McCall all vanished from the Levitt home overnight. Their cars were still in the driveway, their purses inside. The porch light's glass globe was broken.

name: Holly Piirainen
summary: Ten-year-old Holly Piirainen disappeared while visiting grandparents in Sturbridge, Massachusetts. Her skeleton was found in a wooded area in 1993. A shoe of hers was found near where a man named Robert Sousa lived.

name: Polly Klaas
summary: Twelve-year-old Polly Klaas was kidnapped at knifepoint from a slumber party at her Petaluma home and murdered. Richard Allen Davis was convicted and sentenced to death.

name: Steve Branch, Michael Moore & Christopher Byers
summary: Three eight-year-old boys were murdered in West Memphis, Arkansas. Three teenagers — Damien Echols, Jason Baldwin, and Jessie Misskelley Jr. — were convicted but released in 2011 via Alford pleas.

name: Crystal Ann Tymich
summary: Six-year-old Crystal Ann Tymich disappeared from South Los Angeles on June 30, 1994. She was playing outside when she vanished. Despite extensive searches and FBI involvement, Crystal has never been found.

name: Dr. John Bayard Britton
summary: Abortion provider Dr. John Britton and his clinic escort James Barrett were shot dead outside a Pensacola clinic by anti-abortion activist Paul Jennings Hill.

name: Lamar Johnson (Exoneration)
summary: Marcus Boyd was murdered in St. Louis in 1994. Lamar Johnson was wrongfully convicted and spent 28 years in prison before being exonerated in 2023 after the St.

name: Melissa Witt
summary: Nineteen-year-old Melissa Witt was abducted from a bowling alley parking lot in Fort Smith, Arkansas. Her body was found weeks later in a forest. Despite decades of investigation, her killer has never been identified.

name: Nicole Brown Simpson & Ron Goldman
summary: Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman were stabbed to death outside her Brentwood condominium. Nicole's ex-husband O.J. Simpson was tried for the murders in the 'Trial of the Century' and acquitted in 1995.

name: Deanna Cremin
summary: Seventeen-year-old Deanna Cremin was found strangled in an alleyway in Somerville, Massachusetts. She had last been seen leaving a birthday party. Despite investigation, her killer was never identified.

name: Jodi Huisentruit
summary: Television news anchor Jodi Huisentruit disappeared on her way to work at KIMT-TV in Mason City, Iowa. Her car was found with signs of a struggle.

name: Oklahoma City Bombing Victims
summary: The bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building killed 168 people and injured hundreds more. Timothy McVeigh and Terry Nichols were convicted; McVeigh was executed in 2001.

name: Amber Hagerman
summary: Nine-year-old Amber Hagerman was abducted while riding her bicycle in an Arlington parking lot. A neighbor saw a man pull her into his truck. Her body was found four days later in a drainage ditch.

name: Cayce Lynn McDaniel
summary: Fourteen-year-old Cayce Lynn McDaniel disappeared from Milan, Tennessee in May 1996. She was last seen near her home. Despite years of investigation and FBI involvement, she has never been found and no one has been charged.

name: JonBenét Ramsey
summary: Six-year-old beauty pageant winner found dead in the basement of her family's home on the morning after Christmas. A ransom note demanding $118,000 was found, but JonBenét had never left the house.

name: Kristin Smart
summary: Cal Poly freshman Kristin Smart disappeared after a party near campus. Fellow student Paul Flores was the last person seen with her.

name: Julianne Williams & Lollie Winans
summary: Julianne Williams and Laura 'Lollie' Winans were found murdered at their backcountry campsite in Shenandoah National Park in 1996.

name: Tupac Shakur
summary: Rapper Tupac Shakur was shot multiple times in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas after attending a boxing match. He died six days later at University Medical Center of Nevada.

name: Amy Bechtel
summary: Twenty-four-year-old Amy Bechtel disappeared while jogging on a mountain road near Lander, Wyoming. Her car was found at a trailhead. Despite extensive searches and investigation, Amy has never been found.

name: Ennis Cosby
summary: Ennis Cosby, son of Bill Cosby, was shot while changing a tire on Interstate 405 in Los Angeles. Mikhail Markhasev was convicted of the murder in 1998. The case shocked the entertainment world.

name: Gianni Versace
summary: Fashion designer Gianni Versace was shot on the steps of his Miami Beach mansion by spree killer Andrew Cunanan. Cunanan had already killed four others across the country before targeting Versace.

name: Kristen Modafferi
summary: Eighteen-year-old Kristen Modafferi disappeared from San Francisco while working a summer job before starting at UC San Diego. She was last seen on a bus.

name: Michelle Moore-Bosko
summary: Eighteen-year-old Michelle Moore-Bosko was raped and murdered in her Norfolk apartment. Four Navy sailors — the 'Norfolk Four' — were coerced into false confessions and convicted.

name: Peter Boy Kema
summary: Six-year-old Peter Boy Kema disappeared from Hilo, Hawaii in January 1997. His parents were convicted of murder in absentia as his body was never found. The case drew attention to child abuse and neglect on the Big Island.

name: The Notorious B.I.G. (Christopher Wallace)
summary: Rapper Christopher Wallace, known as The Notorious B.I.G., was shot in a drive-by shooting in Los Angeles after attending the Soul Train Music Awards. He was killed just six months after Tupac Shakur.

name: James Byrd Jr.
summary: James Byrd Jr., a Black man, was chained to a pickup truck and dragged to his death in Jasper, Texas by three white supremacists. John William King and Lawrence Russell Brewer were executed; Shawn Berry received a life sentence.

name: Hae Min Lee
summary: High school student Hae Min Lee was strangled and her body found in Leakin Park, Baltimore. Her ex-boyfriend Adnan Syed was convicted of first-degree murder in 2000. His case became the subject of the blockbuster Serial podcast.

name: Yosemite Sightseer Murders
summary: Carole Sund, her daughter Juli, and friend Silvina Pelosso went missing near Yosemite and were found dead weeks later. Handyman Cary Stayner was convicted of their murders plus a fourth victim, a park ranger interpreter.

name: Asha Degree
summary: Nine-year-old Asha Degree left her family home in the early morning hours during a storm and was last seen walking along Highway 18. Her bookbag was found buried in a construction site 26 miles away over a year later.

name: Molly Bish
summary: Sixteen-year-old Molly Bish disappeared from her lifeguard post at Comins Pond in Warren, Massachusetts. Only her swimsuit, sandals, and a shoe were found. Her skeletal remains were discovered three years later in the woods.

name: Valerie Mack
summary: Valerie Mack's remains were found in Manorville, Long Island in 2000 and later in Ocean Parkway among other Gilgo Beach victims. She was identified in 2020 via DNA. She may be a victim of the Long Island Serial Killer.

name: Bonny Lee Bakley
summary: Bonny Lee Bakley was shot while sitting in actor Robert Blake's parked car outside a restaurant in Studio City, Los Angeles. Blake claimed he had gone back to the restaurant to retrieve a gun.

name: Chandra Levy
summary: Federal intern Chandra Levy disappeared from Washington D.C. in 2001. Her remains were found in Rock Creek Park a year later. Her disappearance drew enormous attention due to her relationship with congressman Gary Condit.

name: Duran Bailey
summary: Duran Bailey was brutally beaten and stabbed to death in a Las Vegas field in July 2001, becoming the center of a landmark wrongful conviction case.

name: Henryk Siwiak
summary: Henryk Siwiak, a Polish immigrant, was shot and killed in Brooklyn on the same night as the 9/11 attacks. Because all police resources were diverted to the World Trade Center, the crime scene was not properly processed.

name: Jill-Lyn Euto
summary: College student Jill-Lyn Euto was found stabbed to death in her Syracuse, New York apartment in May 2001. No arrests were made in the case. Her murder remains open with Syracuse Police.

name: Kent Heitholt
summary: Columbia Tribune sports editor Kent Heitholt was beaten and strangled in the Tribune parking lot. Two men were convicted — Ryan Ferguson and Charles Erickson — but Ferguson's conviction was vacated in 2013 after key witness…

name: Thomas C. Wales
summary: Federal prosecutor Thomas Wales, also known for his gun control advocacy, was shot through the window of his home-office in Seattle by a single bullet. A suspect was identified but never charged due to insufficient evidence.

name: Alexis Patterson
summary: Seven-year-old Alexis Patterson disappeared near her Milwaukee school on the same day Elizabeth Smart was abducted in Utah. Alexis's disappearance received far less media coverage, sparking national conversation about racial…

name: Ariel Castro Victims
summary: Michelle Knight, Amanda Berry, and Gina DeJesus were individually abducted and held captive for about a decade in Ariel Castro's Cleveland home. Amanda Berry escaped in 2013 with her daughter born in captivity.

name: Daniel Pearl
summary: Wall Street Journal reporter Daniel Pearl was kidnapped and murdered in Pakistan in 2002. Omar Sheikh was convicted in Pakistan. Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh's death sentence was overturned in 2021 by Pakistan's Supreme Court.

name: Danielle van Dam
summary: Seven-year-old Danielle van Dam was abducted from her Sabre Springs home and murdered by neighbor David Westerfield. Her body was found in a rural area two months later. Westerfield was convicted and sentenced to death.

name: Elizabeth Smart
summary: Fourteen-year-old Elizabeth Smart was abducted from her Salt Lake City bedroom by Brian David Mitchell and his wife. She was held captive for nine months, often in plain sight. She was rescued after being recognized in public.

name: Samantha Runnion
summary: Five-year-old Samantha Runnion was abducted from outside her Orange County apartment complex and murdered. Her mother Erin Runnion became a prominent child safety advocate, founding the Joyful Child Foundation.

name: John Gilbride
summary: John Gilbride, involved in a bitter custody dispute with members of the MOVE organization, was shot and killed in his car in Maple Shade, New Jersey.

name: Laci Peterson
summary: Laci Peterson was eight months pregnant when she disappeared on Christmas Eve. Her husband Scott Peterson reported her missing and became the prime suspect.

name: Rachel Louise Cooke
summary: Nineteen-year-old Rachel Cooke went for a morning jog near her parents' home during winter break from college and never returned. A neighbor saw a truck driving slowly behind her.

name: Sara Ann Lewis Trusty
summary: Sara Ann Trusty disappeared while biking near her church in the Galveston County area. Her body was found days later in a local reservoir. Despite investigation, the killer has never been identified or arrested.

name: Shawn Hornbeck
summary: Eleven-year-old Shawn Hornbeck was abducted while riding his bike in Richwoods, Missouri. He was held captive for four and a half years by Michael Devlin in a nearby town.

name: Blue Ridge Savings Bank Murders
summary: Three bank employees were found dead in the utility room of a Blue Ridge Savings Bank in Greer, South Carolina. Sylvia Holtzclaw, James 'Eb' Barnes, and Margaret 'Maggie' Barnes were all killed.

name: Dru Sjodin
summary: University of North Dakota student Dru Sjodin was abducted from a mall parking lot in Grand Forks by registered sex offender Alfonso Rodriguez Jr. Her body was found in Minnesota.

name: Jason Johnson (Camoflauge)
summary: Rapper Jason Johnson, known as Camoflauge, was shot and killed in Savannah, Georgia near his car. He was found by his young daughter. Despite a reward offered for information, his murder remains unsolved.

name: Tamara Greene
summary: Tamara Greene, known as 'Strawberry,' was an exotic dancer found shot to death in her car in Detroit. Theories linked her death to a party she allegedly attended at the Manoogian Mansion involving Mayor Kwame Kilpatrick.

name: Terrence Williams & Felipe Santos
summary: Terrence Williams and Felipe Santos both separately disappeared after being given rides by Collier County Sheriff's Deputy Steve Calkins, who dropped them at their destinations according to his account.

name: Todd Kohlhepp Victims
summary: Real estate agent Todd Kohlhepp was identified as a serial killer after a chained survivor was found on his rural South Carolina property in 2016.

name: Carlie Brucia
summary: Eleven-year-old Carlie Brucia was abducted from a car wash in Sarasota on Super Bowl Sunday while walking home. Surveillance footage of her abduction was broadcast nationally. Joseph P.

name: Maura Murray
summary: UMass Amherst student Maura Murray crashed her car on a remote road in New Hampshire and vanished before help arrived. A witness offered assistance but she declined.

name: Jeff Davis 8 Victims
summary: Eight women and girls were found dead in and around Jefferson Davis Parish over several years. Many were involved in prostitution or drug use.

name: Jessica Lunsford
summary: Nine-year-old Jessica Lunsford was abducted from her Homosassa home and murdered by registered sex offender John Couey. Her remains were found in a bag buried near Couey's trailer. She had been buried alive.

name: Natalee Holloway
summary: Alabama teenager Natalee Holloway disappeared while on a graduation trip to Aruba. She was last seen leaving a bar with Joran van der Sloot, who was investigated repeatedly but not charged in her disappearance.

name: Teresa Halbach
summary: Freelance photographer Teresa Halbach disappeared after photographing a vehicle at the Avery Salvage Yard. Her remains were found on the property. Steven Avery and his nephew Brendan Dassey were both convicted of murder.

name: Cassie Jo Stoddart
summary: Sixteen-year-old Cassie Jo Stoddart was murdered while alone housesitting in Pocatello, Idaho. Brian Draper and Torey Adamcik were convicted of her murder.

name: Jennifer Kesse
summary: Twenty-four-year-old Jennifer Kesse disappeared from her Orlando condominium complex. Surveillance footage captured an unidentified person driving her car.

name: Nina Reiser
summary: Nina Reiser, a Russian-born woman, disappeared in Oakland, California. Her estranged husband Hans Reiser, a prominent open-source software developer, was convicted of first-degree murder in 2008.

name: Anthony Sowell Victims
summary: Anthony Sowell was convicted of murdering 11 women in Cleveland whose bodies were found in and around his home in 2009. He preyed on vulnerable women in his neighborhood.

name: Chris Benoit Family Murders
summary: Professional wrestler Chris Benoit murdered his wife Nancy and seven-year-old son Daniel in their Fayetteville, Georgia home over a weekend, then hung himself.

name: Long Island Serial Killer Victims
summary: The skeletal remains of 10 people — mostly female sex workers — were found along Ocean Parkway on Long Island, New York. Known as the Gilgo Beach murders, a serial killer dubbed LISK is believed responsible.

name: Stacy Peterson
summary: Stacy Peterson disappeared from Bolingbrook, Illinois. Her husband Drew Peterson, a former police officer, was suspected. He was later convicted of the separate murder of his third wife Kathleen Savio.

name: Caylee Anthony
summary: Two-year-old Caylee Anthony disappeared in June 2008. Her mother Casey Anthony waited 31 days before reporting her missing. Caylee's skeletal remains were found near the family home in December 2008.

name: Darnell Donerson, Jason Hudson & Julian King
summary: Actress Jennifer Hudson's mother Darnell Donerson, brother Jason Hudson, and seven-year-old nephew Julian King were murdered in their Chicago home.

name: Denise Amber Lee
summary: Twenty-three-year-old Denise Amber Lee was abducted by Michael King from her North Port, Florida home. She called 911 from her abductor's car but dispatchers failed to properly respond. King was convicted and executed in 2024.

name: Amber Dubois
summary: Fourteen-year-old Amber Dubois disappeared while walking to her Escondido high school. Convicted sex offender John Gardner abducted and killed her. He was convicted in 2010 and sentenced to life without parole.

name: Brittanee Drexel
summary: Seventeen-year-old Brittanee Drexel disappeared from Myrtle Beach, South Carolina during spring break in 2009. In 2022, Raymond Moody pleaded guilty to her kidnapping, rape, and murder and was sentenced to life in prison.

name: Oscar Grant
summary: Oscar Grant was shot and killed by BART police officer Johannes Mehserle on the Fruitvale station platform in Oakland. Mehserle claimed he mistook his gun for his Taser.

name: Susan Powell
summary: Susan Powell vanished from her West Valley City, Utah home while her husband Josh claimed to have taken their two young sons camping at night in freezing temperatures.

name: Chelsea King
summary: Seventeen-year-old Chelsea King vanished while jogging near her Rancho Bernardo home. John Gardner was convicted of her murder and linked to Amber Dubois.

name: Kyron Horman
summary: Seven-year-old Kyron Horman vanished from Skyline Elementary School after attending a science fair. His stepmother, Terri Horman, was the last known person to see him.

name: Yeardley Love
summary: University of Virginia lacrosse player Yeardley Love was beaten to death in her Charlottesville apartment by her ex-boyfriend and fellow lacrosse player George Huguely V.

name: Garrett Phillips
summary: Twelve-year-old Garrett Phillips was found strangled in his apartment in Potsdam, New York. His mother's ex-boyfriend, Oral 'Nick' Hillary, was tried for the murder twice but acquitted both times.

name: Holly Bobo
summary: Twenty-year-old nursing student Holly Bobo was abducted near her home in Darden, Tennessee. Her remains were found four years later. Zach Adams was convicted of her murder in 2017 and sentenced to three life terms.

name: Juanita Williams
summary: Juanita Williams was found strangled in Hartford, Connecticut. Despite investigation by Hartford Police, no arrests were made and the case went cold. Her family has continued to seek answers.

name: Lauren Spierer
summary: Twenty-year-old Indiana University student Lauren Spierer disappeared in Bloomington, Indiana after a night out. She was captured on surveillance video in the early morning hours.

name: Leiby Kletzky
summary: Eight-year-old Leiby Kletzky was on his first walk home alone in the Borough Park neighborhood of Brooklyn when he got lost. He asked Levi Aron for directions; Aron abducted and killed him.

name: Lisa Irwin
summary: Ten-month-old Lisa Irwin disappeared from her crib in Kansas City, Missouri. Her parents reported her missing in the early morning hours.

name: Brittany Killgore
summary: Twenty-two-year-old Brittany Killgore disappeared from Lake Elsinore after responding to a Craigslist ad. Her body was found days later.

name: Faith Hedgepeth
summary: UNC Chapel Hill student Faith Hedgepeth was found dead in her apartment after a night out. DNA was recovered but went unmatched for nearly a decade.

name: Jessica Ridgeway
summary: Ten-year-old Jessica Ridgeway was abducted while walking to school in Westminster, Colorado. Her remains were found in pieces over several days.

name: Jordan Davis
summary: Seventeen-year-old Jordan Davis was shot at a Jacksonville gas station by Michael Dunn following an argument over loud music. Dunn fired into the vehicle claiming self-defense.

name: Melissa Jenkins
summary: Melissa Jenkins, a high school teacher, disappeared after stopping to help a car she thought was stranded. Her body was found in a pond. Allen Prue and his wife Patricia Prue were convicted of murder.

name: Abigail Hernandez
summary: Fourteen-year-old Abby Hernandez disappeared while walking home from school in Conway, New Hampshire. She reappeared nearly nine months later, having been held captive by Nathaniel Kibby. Kibby was sentenced to 45 years in prison.

name: Alexis Murphy
summary: Seventeen-year-old Alexis Murphy disappeared after stopping at a gas station in Nelson County, Virginia. Randy Taylor, a convicted sex offender who worked at the gas station, was convicted of her abduction and murder despite her…

name: Avonte Oquendo
summary: Fourteen-year-old autistic student Avonte Oquendo disappeared from his Queens school in October 2013. His remains were found in the East River in January 2014. His death was ruled accidental drowning.

name: Elisa Lam
summary: Canadian tourist Elisa Lam was found dead in a rooftop water tank at the Cecil Hotel in Los Angeles. Eerie elevator surveillance footage showed her behaving oddly before her disappearance.

name: Hanna Harris
summary: Hanna Harris, a Northern Cheyenne tribal member, disappeared on the Fourth of July from the Northern Cheyenne Reservation in Montana. Her body was found a week later. Two men were eventually convicted of her murder.

name: Eric Garner
summary: Eric Garner died after being placed in a chokehold by NYPD officer Daniel Pantaleo during an arrest in Staten Island. His final words 'I can't breathe' became a rallying cry. A Staten Island grand jury declined to indict Pantaleo.

name: Jessica Chambers
summary: Nineteen-year-old Jessica Chambers was found burning on a road in Courtland, Mississippi, her body set on fire while she was still alive. She was able to say a partial name to a first responder but died shortly after.

name: Laquan McDonald
summary: Seventeen-year-old Laquan McDonald was shot 16 times by Chicago police officer Jason Van Dyke. Dashboard camera footage was suppressed for 13 months.

name: Michael Brown
summary: Eighteen-year-old Michael Brown was shot and killed by Ferguson police officer Darren Wilson. A grand jury declined to indict Wilson.

name: Tamir Rice
summary: Twelve-year-old Tamir Rice was shot and killed by Cleveland police officer Timothy Loehmann within two seconds of arriving at a park where Tamir was playing with a toy gun. A grand jury declined to indict the officers.

name: Freddie Gray
summary: Freddie Gray died of spinal cord injuries sustained while in Baltimore police custody. Six officers were charged but all were acquitted or had charges dropped. His death sparked the 2015 Baltimore uprising.

name: Sandra Bland
summary: Sandra Bland was found dead in her Waller County, Texas jail cell three days after a traffic stop arrest. Her death was ruled a suicide by hanging but her family and many others believe she was murdered.

name: Walter Scott
summary: Walter Scott was shot in the back and killed while fleeing from North Charleston police officer Michael Slager during a traffic stop.

name: Ingrid Lyne
summary: Forty-year-old Ingrid Lyne was murdered in Renton, Washington. Her dismembered remains were found in multiple locations including trash bins.

name: Philando Castile
summary: Philando Castile was shot and killed by a police officer during a traffic stop in Falcon Heights, Minnesota. His girlfriend broadcast the aftermath live on Facebook. Officer Jeronimo Yanez was acquitted of manslaughter in 2017.

name: Terri 'Missy' Bevers
summary: Fitness instructor Missy Bevers was found dead in a church where she was preparing for an early morning boot camp class. Surveillance footage showed a suspect in SWAT-style tactical gear walking through the church before the…

name: Tyler & Charlee Worley
summary: Brandi Worley stabbed her two young children Tyler (7) and Charlee (3) to death in their Darlington, Indiana home. She then stabbed herself. She told her husband 'you'll never take the kids from me' before the murders.

name: Abigail Williams & Liberty German
summary: Thirteen-year-old Abigail Williams and fourteen-year-old Liberty German were murdered while hiking the Monon High Bridge Trail. Liberty managed to record audio and video of a suspect on her phone.

name: Richard Allen Conviction (Delphi)
summary: Richard Allen was convicted in November 2024 for the murders of Abigail Williams and Liberty German on the Monon High Bridge Trail. The conviction came after a tumultuous legal process including judge recusals and controversy.

name: Savanna LaFontaine-Greywind
summary: Twenty-two-year-old Savanna LaFontaine-Greywind was eight months pregnant when she was murdered in Fargo, North Dakota. Her neighbors Brooke Crews and William Hoehn were convicted of her murder.

name: Botham Jean
summary: Botham Jean was shot in his own apartment by off-duty Dallas Police officer Amber Guyger, who claimed she entered his apartment by mistake. Guyger was convicted of murder in 2019 and sentenced to 10 years.

name: Shanann Watts & Family
summary: Shanann Watts and her two young daughters Bella and Celeste were murdered by her husband Chris Watts in Frederick, Colorado. He also killed their unborn son.

name: Dulce Maria Alavez
summary: Five-year-old Dulce Maria Alavez disappeared from a playground at Bridgeton City Park while her mother sat in a nearby car. A witness reported seeing a man lead the child away.

name: Elizabeth Barraza
summary: Elizabeth Barraza was shot in her own driveway at 6:55 AM while setting up for a garage sale. A doorbell camera captured the suspect approaching her disguised as a delivery person.

name: Jennifer Dulos
summary: Jennifer Dulos disappeared from her New Canaan, Connecticut home. Her estranged husband Fotis Dulos and his girlfriend Michelle Troconis were arrested. Fotis Dulos died by suicide in 2020 before trial.

name: Tylee Ryan & Joshua 'JJ' Vallow
summary: Seventeen-year-old Tylee Ryan and seven-year-old JJ Vallow disappeared and were later found buried in the backyard of their mother's new husband Chad Daybell. Their mother Lori Vallow and Daybell were convicted of their murders.

name: Breonna Taylor
summary: EMT Breonna Taylor was shot and killed by police executing a no-knock warrant at her Louisville apartment. No drugs were found. Her boyfriend fired at officers believing it was a break-in.

name: George Floyd
summary: George Floyd died after Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck for over nine minutes. His death sparked worldwide protests and the Black Lives Matter movement.

name: Suzanne Morphew
summary: Suzanne Morphew disappeared on Mother's Day in Chaffee County, Colorado. Her husband Barry Morphew was arrested in 2021 and charged with murder. Charges were dismissed in 2022 due to prosecutorial misconduct.

name: Gabrielle Petito
summary: Travel blogger Gabrielle Petito was strangled and found in Grand Teton National Park, Wyoming. Her fiancé Brian Laundrie returned home alone and refused to cooperate with investigators before fleeing.

name: Miya Marcano
summary: Nineteen-year-old college student Miya Marcano disappeared from her apartment complex in Orange County, Florida where she worked.

name: Ethan Chapin
summary: University of Idaho freshman Ethan Chapin was murdered with three classmates in their off-campus house. He was visiting his girlfriend Xana Kernodle. Bryan Kohberger was arrested in Pennsylvania and faces murder charges.

name: Idaho Student Murders
summary: Four University of Idaho students — Ethan Chapin, Xana Kernodle, Madison Mogen, and Kaylee Goncalves — were stabbed to death in their off-campus house in Moscow, Idaho.

name: Kaylee Goncalves
summary: University of Idaho student Kaylee Goncalves was one of four students murdered in their off-campus house in Moscow, Idaho. Bryan Kohberger was arrested in December 2022.

name: Madison Mogen
summary: University of Idaho student Madison Mogen was one of four students murdered in their off-campus house in Moscow, Idaho. Bryan Kohberger was arrested and awaits trial. Madison and Kaylee Goncalves were found in the same bed.

name: Xana Kernodle
summary: University of Idaho junior Xana Kernodle was murdered with three classmates in their off-campus house. Her boyfriend Ethan Chapin was also killed. Bryan Kohberger, a criminology PhD student, was arrested in December 2022.

name: Ana Walshe
summary: Ana Walshe's dismembered remains were found in the trash after she disappeared from her Cohasset, Massachusetts home. Her husband Brian Walshe was arrested and charged with murder.

name: Ashley Loring HeavyRunner
summary: Ashley Loring HeavyRunner, a 20-year-old Blackfeet Community College student, vanished from the Blackfeet Indian Reservation in Browning, Montana, in June 2017.

name: Barbara Louise Cotton
summary: Fifteen-year-old Barbara Louise Cotton vanished on the evening of April 11, 1981, after leaving a restaurant on Main Street in Williston, North Dakota, and walking toward Recreation Park, blocks from her home.

name: Bear Brook Murders (Allenstown Four)
summary: In 1985 and 2000, the remains of a woman and three young girls were found in barrels near Bear Brook State Park in Allenstown, New Hampshire; all four had died of blunt force trauma.

name: Katherine Ann Alston (Bedford Jane Doe)
summary: On October 6, 1971, the decomposing body of a young woman was found off a logging road in a wooded area of Bedford, New Hampshire.

name: York County Jane Doe (Biddeford Jane Doe)
summary: On July 25, 2009, the cranium of a teenage girl or young woman was found wrapped in seaweed near the tide line on a beach in Biddeford, Maine.

name: Brandon Victor Swanson
summary: Brandon Swanson, 19, drove his car into a ditch on rural roads near Lynd, Minnesota, in the early hours of May 14, 2008, while driving home to Marshall.

name: Carlene Brown
summary: Carlene Brown, 19, disappeared from the Little Britches Rodeo in Rawlins, Wyoming, on July 4, 1974, along with her friend Christine "Christy" Gross.

name: DeOrr Kunz Jr.
summary: Two-year-old DeOrr Jay Kunz Jr. vanished on July 10, 2015, from Timber Creek Campground in remote Lemhi County, Idaho, about ten miles from Leadore, while camping with his parents, great-grandfather, and a family friend.

name: Patricia 'Trisha' Meleady Newsom (East Haven Jane Doe)
summary: On August 16, 1975, a truck driver found the body of a young woman — bound, gagged, and wrapped in a tarp — in a drainage ditch behind the Bradlees department store on Frontage Road in East Haven, Connecticut.

name: Erin Marie Gilbert
summary: Erin Marie Gilbert, a 24-year-old Anchorage nanny, vanished from the Girdwood Forest Fair in Girdwood, Alaska, on July 1, 1995, while on a first date.

name: Eugene Wade Martin
summary: Eugene Wade Martin, a 13-year-old Des Moines Register carrier, vanished in the early morning of August 12, 1984, while delivering Sunday papers on Des Moines' south side; only his bag of rolled newspapers was found at his pickup…

name: Florence Okpealuk
summary: Florence Okpealuk, a 33-year-old Inupiaq mother originally from Wales, Alaska, was last seen on August 31, 2020, leaving a tent on West Beach about one to two miles outside Nome.

name: Lily Janelle (Frenchville Baby Jane Doe)
summary: On December 7, 1985, a dog carried the frozen body of a newborn girl from a gravel pit in Frenchville, Maine, to a nearby home. The infant, known for decades as Baby Jane Doe, was identified through genetic genealogy in 2022…

name: Patricia Ann Tucker ("Granby Girl")
summary: On November 15, 1978, the skeletal remains of a woman who had been shot in the temple were found buried under leaves off a logging road in Granby, Massachusetts.

name: Jason Jolkowski
summary: Jason Anthony Jolkowski, 19, vanished on the morning of June 13, 2001, while walking about eight blocks from his Omaha home toward Benson High School, where a coworker was to pick him up for a shift at a nearby restaurant.

name: Jermain Charlo
summary: Jermain Charlo, a 23-year-old mother of two and enrolled member of the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes, was last seen around midnight on June 15-16, 2018, on surveillance video in an alley behind the Badlander bar in…

name: Jessie Foster
summary: Jessica "Jessie" Foster, a 21-year-old Canadian woman from Kamloops, British Columbia, was last heard from by telephone at her North Las Vegas residence on March 28, 2006.

name: Joshua Guimond
summary: Joshua Guimond, a 20-year-old junior at Saint John's University in Collegeville, Minnesota, left a late-night card game at the Metten Court dormitory around 11:45 p.m.

name: Kevin Ives & Don Henry (Boys on the Tracks)
summary: In the early morning of August 23, 1987, 17-year-old Kevin Ives and 16-year-old Don Henry were run over by a Union Pacific freight train near Alexander in Saline County, Arkansas, their bodies lying motionless and partly covered…

name: Ruth Marie Terry (Lady of the Dunes)
summary: On July 26, 1974, the mutilated body of a woman was found in the Race Point dunes of Cape Cod National Seashore in Provincetown, Massachusetts.

name: LeeAnna Warner
summary: Five-year-old LeeAnna Warner vanished on June 14, 2003, while walking home from a friend's house about a block away in Chisholm, Minnesota.

name: Leigh Marine Occhi
summary: Thirteen-year-old Leigh Occhi vanished from her Tupelo, Mississippi home on the morning of August 27, 1992, as remnants of Hurricane Andrew moved through the area.

name: Marc Allen
summary: Thirteen-year-old Marc James-Warren Allen II vanished on March 29, 1986, after telling his mother he was walking to a friend's house near his home on Emma Avenue on Des Moines' south side.

name: Michael Joseph Vaughan
summary: Michael Joseph 'Monkey' Vaughan, age 5, disappeared from near his home in Fruitland, Idaho, on the evening of July 27, 2021, and despite years of extensive searches his body has never been found.

name: New Bedford Highway Killer Victims
summary: Between March 1988 and April 1989, eleven women with ties to New Bedford, Massachusetts, vanished; the bodies of nine were found dumped along Route 140, Interstate 195, and nearby roads, while two women were never found.

name: New Britain Jane Doe
summary: On October 11, 1991, a survey crew found the badly decomposed body of a woman in garbage bags near railroad tracks off Myrtle Street in New Britain, Connecticut, across from the former Fafnir Bearing plant.

name: Matthew Isaac Doe (Northfield Baby Boy Doe)
summary: On April 1, 1982, schoolchildren waiting for a bus in Northfield, Vermont, found a deceased newborn boy inside a plastic garbage bag after a dog dragged it along the road.

name: Rachel Lucille Cyriacks
summary: Rachel Cyriacks, a 30-year-old mother of three from Woonsocket, South Dakota, vanished on November 13, 2013, after driving to Huron to pick up her estranged husband, Brad Cyriacks, who was being released from jail.

name: Randy Leach
summary: Randy Wayne Leach, a 17-year-old high school senior from Linwood, Kansas, disappeared in the early morning hours of April 16, 1988, after attending a pre-graduation party in rural Leavenworth County.

name: Serenity June Dennard
